claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Based on my review of the official UK government guidance, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**The main issue:** You do not live in the UK, which is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

According to the official guidance, "You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK."

While you meet several other important criteria:
- ✓ Alex is 9 years old (under 16)
- ✓ You contribute £30.00 per week towards Alex's upkeep (enough to demonstrate responsibility)
- ✓ No other claimant has priority
- ✓ Alex is not in care, hospital, or any disqualifying situation

**However**, the UK residency requirement is essential. The guidance does mention limited exceptions for:
- Crown servants (government employees working abroad)
- Those living in certain specific countries with reciprocal agreements
- Those with settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

Since you don't fall under any of these specific exceptions, you cannot claim Child Benefit while living outside the UK.

The child is not in local authority care, hospital, or residential accommodation, and does not meet any of the disqualifying factors (not working 24+ hours/week, no apprenticeship, no qualifying benefits). While the claimant is contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards Alex's upkeep (which typically would allow continued eligibility when a child lives elsewhere), the critical disqualifying factor is that the claimant does not live in the UK. According to the official guidance, 'You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK.' The guidance does mention that 'You may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant' and discusses various exceptions for those with settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, but these are specific exceptions. The baseline requirement is UK residency. Since the claimant does not live in the UK and there is no indication they fall under any of the specific exceptions (Crown servant, certain countries with reciprocal arrangements, or EU Settlement Scheme status), they do not meet the fundamental residency requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.
